output.brief: The rise in Corvane's mishandled bags is not mainly a handler problem. Since 1 September, tags printed on the new Fennick stock fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against 1.5% before. The failed bags go to the manual encode desk and reach the make-up lateral after it has closed. Bags on the automatic-read path stayed at about 3.8 per 1,000. Pelion uses the same Tessaly crew pool and stayed flat at about 3.7. In mid-October, counters that briefly used old Brackwater stock read at 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick stock still failed at 12%. So the stock change is the trigger. I can't tell whether the Fennick media is defective or just needs different printer heat settings, so a defect claim against Fennick is premature. Don't issue the breach notice or withhold Tessaly's fee, because the evidence points away from them. Switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater now. About five weeks of stock is in stores and the contract runs to 31 Dec. Then test Fennick with the printer vendor's settings. Asking HBAA for an extra encode workstation in the evening bank is a reasonable stopgap. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis. The printer-jam link and the defect question remain open.
